root_cause.text: In drm/msm VM_BIND UNMAP handling, vm_bind_job_lock_objects() passed op->obj_offset instead of the unmap range to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock(), causing the wrong object set to be locked and leaving non-_NO_SHARE BO reservation objects unlocked during UNMAP.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the UNMAP call in drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_gem_vma.c from `drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock(job->vm, exec, op->iova, op->obj_offset)` to `... op->range)`, and the commit message states that a “Wrong argument meant that the objs involved in UNMAP ops were not always getting locked,” with impact visible for “non-_NO_SHARE BOs.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix VM unmap locking to use the unmap range instead of the object offset.
intent_record.what: In vm_bind_job_lock_objects(), the argument passed to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock() for the MSM_VM_BIND_OP_UNMAP case was changed from op->obj_offset to op->range, while leaving the other arguments unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, unmap operations now use the requested range/length value instead of an object offset when locking and preparing the GPU virtual memory unmap, preventing the unmap path from operating on the wrong extent and making the unmap behavior match the intended request.

grouping_result.intent: Fix VM unmap locking to use the unmap range instead of the object offset.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes VM_BIND UNMAP locking by using the unmap range rather than op->obj_offset when determining which objects to lock.

candidates.rationale: This is the call site that performs UNMAP locking. Per the root cause, this invocation passes the wrong argument set for the unmap range, leading to incorrect object locking during UNMAP.

This argument is the direct root cause: op->obj_offset was passed as the unmap range parameter instead of the actual unmap length/range, so the wrong BOs were locked and some reservation objects remained unlocked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This exact argument is the root cause: vm_bind_job_lock_objects() passed op->obj_offset to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock() for UNMAP locking, instead of the actual unmap range/length, causing the wrong object set to be locked and leaving some reservation objects unlocked.

This is the UNMAP locking call site where the incorrect argument was supplied. The vulnerability manifests through this invocation because it performs the object locking using the wrong parameter set for the unmap operation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function body is sufficient because it directly contains the VM_BIND object-locking logic for UNMAP. In `vm_bind_job_lock_objects()`, the UNMAP case calls `drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock(job->vm, exec, op->iova, op->obj_offset);`. Per the root cause, this helper must be given the unmap range, but this code passes `op->obj_offset` as the fourth argument instead of `op->range`. The same struct is populated earlier with both fields (`job->ops[i].obj_offset = op->obj_offset;` and `job->ops[i].range = op->range;`), so the correct range value is available but not used here. This means the wrong object set can be locked during UNMAP, leaving some non-`_NO_SHARE` BO reservation objects unlocked. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The relevant logic is fully visible in `vm_bind_job_lock_objects()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause says UNMAP locking passed `op->obj_offset` instead of the unmap range to `drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock()`. That exact vulnerable construct is present here under `case MSM_VM_BIND_OP_UNMAP:`:

`ret = drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock(job->vm, exec, op->iova, op->obj_offset);`

The function is using `op->obj_offset` as the fourth argument for an UNMAP operation, while the operation structure clearly stores the unmap length in `op->range` (set in `lookup_op()` via `job->ops[i].range = op->range;`), and the actual unmap path later uses `op->range` for unmapping in `vm_bind_job_prepare()`:

`ret = drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap(job->vm, &arg, op->iova, op->range);`

So the lock phase and the execution phase disagree: lock uses `obj_offset`, actual unmap uses `range`. This matches the described bug of locking the wrong object set for UNMAP, leaving some BO reservation objects unlocked. There is no corrected call using `op->range` in `vm_bind_job_lock_objects()`, so the fix is not present.
